Plan the size of a precision study by simulation

Source: R/plan.R
msa_plan.Rd

How many items, prompt variants, models and replicates does a study need before the estimated percent gauge R&R can be trusted? With few prompt or model levels the variance components of these factors are estimated with large uncertainty, and the fit is often singular. This function simulates studies of candidate sizes from assumed variance components, refits each one and summarises the distribution of the estimated %GRR (percent study variation) around its true value.

Usage

msa_plan(
  scenarios,
  vc = list(item = 1, prompt = 0.05, model = 0.05, residual = 0.1),
  nsim = 100,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

scenarios

A data.frame with columns n_items, n_prompts, n_models, n_reps (and optionally n_blocks), one row per candidate design.

vc

Assumed variance components, see msa_simulate().

nsim

Simulations per scenario.

seed

Optional seed.

verbose

Print progress.

Value

A data.frame of class msa_plan with, per scenario, the true %GRR, the mean and the 2.5 %, 50 % and 97.5 % quantiles of the estimates, the root-mean-square error, the share of singular fits and the share of simulations that misclassify the system relative to the 10 % / 30 % thresholds.

Examples

# \donttest{
sc <- expand.grid(n_items = c(20, 40), n_prompts = c(3, 6), n_models = 3, n_reps = 3)
msa_plan(sc, vc = list(item = 1, prompt = 0.05, model = 0.05, residual = 0.1),
         nsim = 20, seed = 1)
#> scenario 1/4: 20 items, 3 prompts, 3 models, 3 reps, 1 block(s)
#> scenario 2/4: 40 items, 3 prompts, 3 models, 3 reps, 1 block(s)
#> scenario 3/4: 20 items, 6 prompts, 3 models, 3 reps, 1 block(s)
#> scenario 4/4: 40 items, 6 prompts, 3 models, 3 reps, 1 block(s)
#> Study-size planning by simulation (20 simulations per scenario)
#>   true %GRR (study variation) under the assumed variance components: 40.8 %
#>  n_items n_prompts n_models n_reps n_blocks mean q2.5 median q97.5 rmse
#>       20         3        3      3        1 41.0 29.2   39.9  58.3  8.7
#>       40         3        3      3        1 41.3 32.8   38.9  54.3  6.4
#>       20         6        3      3        1 41.1 28.8   40.2  54.5  6.8
#>       40         6        3      3        1 40.6 32.6   40.3  51.4  5.1
#>  pct_singular pct_misclassified
#>          85.0               5.0
#>          80.0               0.0
#>          85.0               5.0
#>         100.0               0.0
# }
